problems.form_value: Completed the same two creative tasks by themselves on all days
problems.source_says: Minor. The control arm did the two tasks (AUT and product problem-solving) by themselves on Days 1 to 7 only. The Day 30 follow-up survey gave one new AUT (sponge) and no Task 2: Table 2b has no Day 30 row, Table 3 shows '/' for Task 2 at Day30, and p. 24 counts 8 AUT tasks but 7 product tasks. The treatment-arm description counts Day 30 as one of the days, so 'on all days' overstates Day 30. The p. 5 sentence about 'the same two creative tasks' covers Days 2 to 6. The no-AI coding of the arm is right. Suggested wording: 'Completed the same two creative tasks as the treatment group, by themselves, on Days 1 to 7, and one AUT (sponge) without ChatGPT in the Day 30 follow-up survey.'
problems.quote: One month later (label as Day 30), in the follow-up survey where participants were invited to complete another AUT task (i.e., sponge)

summary: The PDF supports every core part of the assignment coding: after consent, the 61 students were randomly assigned at boarding, before the Day 1 baseline, to ChatGPT 4.0 help on their own AUT and product problem-solving tasks on Days 2 to 6 (n = 31) or to doing the same tasks by themselves (n = 30), in a preregistered, individual, between-subjects lab design with no within-person contrast (pp. 3-5, Figure 1). The coding is refuted only on one minor wording point: the control-arm description says the control did 'the same two creative tasks' 'on all days', but the Day 30 follow-up gave one new AUT (sponge) and no Task 2 (p. 7, Tables 2b and 3).
